mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 for three consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >100000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer demand and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.4% month-over-month for three consecutive months, it signals persistent inflation, prompting expectations of future rate hikes and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows at more than 150,000 per month for two consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which may prompt restrictive monetary policy and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS > 150000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary signal, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other macro conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of episodes where two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines occur.
